conflicts.permit: To provide troubleshooting and customer support, we may need to access your information, such as your account email address.
conflicts.prohibit: On the server, your data is protected and not viewed or analyzed in any way.
conflicts.situation: A user with synchronization enabled requests troubleshooting, and isoTimer staff access the user's events, tasks, or notes stored on the server.
conflicts.reason: The support statement permits access to user information, while the server statement says synced data is never viewed. Neither statement names an exception for support access, and the policy states no precedence.

conflicts.permit: We will not disclose your information to law enforcement or other governmental authorities unless we believe it is required to comply with warrants, court orders or other lawful government requests.
conflicts.prohibit: Your data is not shared with any third parties.
conflicts.situation: A court order requests a user's synced events, notes, and contacts stored on the isoTimer server.
conflicts.reason: The no-sharing statement has no legal exception, while the later statement allows disclosure to authorities under legal compulsion. The policy does not link the two statements or say which governs.

conflicts.permit: We may use your Personal Information to contact you with newsletters, marketing or promotional materials.
conflicts.prohibit: We use your Personal Information only for providing and improving the mobile application.
conflicts.situation: MeetHub uses a user's name and contact details to send marketing or promotional newsletters.
conflicts.reason: Marketing outreach is neither providing nor improving the application, and the purpose limitation lists no exception for marketing. The policy gives no precedence between the two statements.

conflicts.permit: Personal Information that we collect may be transferred to, and stored at, any of our affiliates, partners or service providers which may be inside or outside the country you resides in / Economic area your country is part of.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not share or disclose such information and can only be used for suggestions and marketing activities.
conflicts.situation: A user imports an address book, and 10times stores the imported contacts with a hosting provider or transfers them to an affiliate or partner.
conflicts.reason: The contacts statement forbids any sharing or disclosure, while the transfer statement covers all collected personal information. The policy does not say whether imported contacts are excluded from transfers to affiliates, partners, or service providers.

conflicts.permit: we use it to enhance your experience with opportunities like special promotions and offers
conflicts.prohibit: then only we collect the email addresses specifically to send newsletters only about our new app launches.
conflicts.situation: Queleas uses a parent's email address, the main personal information it collects, to send special promotions and offers unrelated to new app launches.
conflicts.reason: One statement uses personal information for promotions and offers, and the other limits email use to newsletters about new app launches. The policy does not say whether promotions fall within those newsletters.

conflicts.permit: Retargeting/advertising cookies collect data about your online activity and identify your interests so that we can provide advertising that we believe is relevant to you.
conflicts.prohibit: Because we collect browsing and persistent identifier data (only for analytic and internal purposes), your selection of the “Do Not Track” option provided by your mobile browser will not have any effect on our collection of analytics information or the collection of a persistent identifier.
conflicts.situation: Genius collects a visitor's browsing activity and persistent identifiers through cookies and uses them to target advertising or sells them to advertisers.
conflicts.reason: The Do Not Track section limits browsing and identifier data to analytic and internal purposes, while the cookie, behavioral advertising, and sale sections use the same data for advertising. No statement says which governs.

conflicts.permit: If you choose to connect your social media account(s), such as Facebook or Twitter, to your user profile on the Service, we display some information from your social media sites on our Service, and such information can include Personal Data.
conflicts.prohibit: We receive certain information related to your Twitter account, such as profile and account information and Twitter accounts you follow, though we do not currently use such information.
conflicts.situation: A user connects a Twitter account to a Genius profile, and Genius displays Twitter profile information on the Service.
conflicts.reason: Displaying Twitter profile information is a use, yet the policy says received Twitter profile and account information is not currently used. The policy does not say which Twitter information is displayed.
